newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SAMPRAS DROPS OUT OF WORLD TEAM CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS DROPS OUT OF WORLD TEAM CUP.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras withdrew from the World Team Cup because of injury on Wednesday but said he would play in the French Open.

Sampras, who retired from his opening match against Australia's Mark Philippoussis on Monday after straining his upper left thigh muscle, was ruled out of the U.S. tie with Croatia but had hoped to play on Friday until doctors advised him to rest the leg.
"I'm not playing this week," said Sampras. "I'm feeling better, I don't feel the injury when I walk but doctors advised me not to come back too soon or I could make it worse.
"I'll hit a few balls and I'm planning on playing in Paris."
Despite the injury, Sampras said he was confident about his chances of claiming the French title, the only grand slam to elude him.
Last year Sampras arrived in Paris under similar circumstances having injured his back at the World Team Cup.
He went to Paris not expecting much and enjoyed his best-ever French Open, reaching the semifinals before losing to eventual champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov.

"I went to Paris last year with no preparation and it's pretty much the same this year," said Sampras, who will leave for the French capital on Thursday. "Last year it sort of worked to my advantage so maybe it will be the same this year.
"I just hope I'm feeling better and over this."
Sampras's clay-court campaign this season has been continually disrupted by injuries.
The World Team Cup was only his third event after missing two tournaments with a wrist injury.
Sampras had been desperate to get in some clay-court competition ahead of the French Open, which begins Monday, after first-round losses in Monte Carlo and the Italian Open.
"I thought I was hitting the ball well here," the Australian Open champion said. "It's just a fluke injury that I have to get over or make the best of."
